title: Raw ask origami and implementation sketch
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a working synthesis of recent customer asks (enterprise + platform teams) where raw voice is still messy. Aim: capture the literal asks, distill a small set of candidate quick-fixes, and sketch minimally-viable implementation paths for eng/product to consider. Not a final decision doc — more like a field notebook for solutions engineering and PM pairing.

How I collected these notes:
- Weekly CS syncs (Mar week 1–2) + 1:1s with 6 accounts flagged by AMs
- Slack search: #cs-enterprise + #priv-deploy-requests (Mar 2027)
- Three customer recordings (redacted quotes below) and relevant ticket threads (see linked Jira keys)

Top line themes (raw):
1) Per-request billing granularity — customers want per-route / per-model billing tags plus clearer post-call attribution when requests route across fallbacks.
2) Private observability gaps — VPC customers missing the same trace/route-level dashboards as hosted (token-level cost attribution, KV cache hit rates, live-tail traces)
3) Explicit cache-control primitives — customers want simple knobs: disable prefix caching for a route, TTL control for KV cache, and a cache diagnostic endpoint.
4) Predictable fallbacks — when primary model is overloaded, customers want deterministic fallback mapping + an option to reject instead of degrade.
5) Quantization & quality toggle — ability to opt certain routes into quantized model variants but keep QA metrics and rollback traces.

Representative raw snippets (anonymized):
- "We had a multi-tenant endpoint and an outage; invoices show tokens but not which product team consumed them — need per-route tags we can reconcile to our internal billing." — Large Fintech AM note
- "Private console feels like a black box compared with hosted — we can’t see cache hit rates and our devs keep asking if a slow request was a cache miss." — Platform eng lead at regulated retailer
- "Fallback to smaller model is fine, but we had a user-facing regression; we need either an allowlist for fallbacks or a hard-fail option." — Conversational AI startup

Initial prioritization (customer-impact x effort rough):
- Low effort, high impact: per-route metadata in billing exports (CSV/BigQuery), cache-diagnostic endpoint (read-only), and documentable default fallback policy.
- Medium effort: per-route toggles for prefix cache, per-model quantization flags with telemetry plumbing.
- Higher effort: full private-console parity for trace-level observability and deterministic fallback orchestration across regions.

Suggested quick-fixes (MVPs to ship in 1–2 sprints):
A) Billing tags in export (MVP):
  - What: Add two new columns to monthly usage export: route_id and route_metadata (free-form tag blob). Allow customers to set route metadata via API/console when creating routes.
  - Why: Enables reconciliation without wholesale billing rewrite. Several accounts requested this immediately.
  - Risk: Some customers will expect real-time dashboards; clarify export latency and SLA in docs.
  - Linked work: JIRA:CS-4821 for schema change; ENG-1312 for export pipeline.

B) Cache-diagnostics endpoint (MVP):
  - What: Read-only HTTP endpoint for private deployments that returns recent cache stats (last 1k requests): overall KV hit rate, prefix cache hit/miss rate, recent eviction count, and example request IDs for misses. Rate-limited and accessible only from management subnet.
  - Why: Lowers support time-to-resolution and reduces noisy tickets.
  - Safety: No PII returned; only request IDs and aggregate counts. Attachable toggle to Private onboarding checklist.

C) Fallback policy: allowlist + hard-fail toggle
  - What: Per-route setting: {fallback_mode: [auto, allowlist, disabled]}; allowlist maps to explicit backup model ids. disabled = do not fallback; return 503.
  - Why: Prevents silent quality regressions and gives customers control over user experience.
  - UX: Expose in console with clear wording and examples, default to auto.

Implementation sketches (engineering notes):
- Billing tags: Small change in route metadata model + enrich usage event pipeline. Events already carry route_id; extend exporter to include route_metadata. Add acceptance test that export CSV contains route tags for mixed-traffic routes. Work scoped to 1 backend engineer + 1 data infra for 2 weeks.

- Cache diagnostics: Instrument runtime to record aggregated counters already present in local metrics. Build a lightweight API handler in control plane that queries the runtime metrics store (Prometheus or in-memory window) and renders JSON. Add RBAC to management plane. Estimate: 1 SRE + 1 runtime dev, 2–3 sprints including security review.

- Fallback policy: Hook into smart router logic. When routing decision happens, check route config. If disabled -> return 503; if allowlist -> route to explicit model; if auto -> current behavior. Add unit tests for routing decision traces; expose fallback decision in trace logs and billing trace so customers can reconcile. Estimate: 2 backend devs, 3 weeks.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- How much history should cache-diagnostics keep? (1k request window seems reasonable but some customers asked for daily aggregates.)
- Billing: do we need to normalize tag schema across teams (enforce k/v pairs) or keep free-form? Free-form is faster but messy for downstream analysis.
- Fallback semantics across dedicated vs hosted: Dedicated customers expect stronger guarantees; do we treat them differently?

Customer impact anecdotes / metrics:
- At least 4 enterprise accounts flagged billing reconciliation as blocking for month-end reporting (potential churn risk if unresolved).
- CS queue shows ~12 tickets in last 30 days mentioning "cache miss / private console" indicating pattern across retail and healthcare customers.

Next recommended steps (practical):
1) Product + Solutions: draft a short-run roadmap with the 3 MVPs above and confirm prioritization with Sales for top-5 named accounts. (Owner: Rhea + Marco)
2) Engineering: quick feasibility spike for cache-diagnostics (2–3 dev-days) to surface metric availability and security gating. (Owner: Ethan)
3) CS: prepare a short FAQ for customers explaining export tagging, expected timeline, and interim workarounds (tag proxying in customer-side logs). (Owner: Janelle)
4) Legal/Security: preflight on no-PII guarantees for diagnostics and confirm data-retention caps.

Appendix — Implementation reference snippets (rough, not for prod):
- Example route metadata payload: {
  "route_id": "acct-123-order-qna",
  "metadata": "team:orders,product:checkout,env:prod"
}
- Example fallback config (YAML):
  route: checkout-qna
  fallback_mode: allowlist
  allowlist_models: ["rw-medium-quant-v2", "rw-small-v1"]

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally scribbly; please comment inline on priority adjustments or if you can commit eng cycles for the spikes.
- If you have concrete customer quotes or tickets I missed, drop them in the linked_artifacts or reply here.

==== end ====
